title: Heterogeneous Chiplet Integration for Flexible AI Workload Execution
problem: Monolithic AI accelerator designs cannot efficiently adapt to varying compute requirements of diverse AI workloads, resulting in suboptimal resource utilization and inefficient performance per watt. Different AI applications require different ratios of GPU, NPU, and CPU compute resources.
motivation: Flexible heterogeneous architectures can better match compute resources to workload characteristics, improving energy efficiency and performance across diverse AI applications.
method: The architecture integrates multiple compute chiplets (GPU, NPU, CPU) connected via a flexible interconnect fabric that dynamically routes data and adapts resource allocation based on workload requirements. The flexible interconnect enables efficient communication between different compute elements to execute diverse AI workloads.
key_novelty: Dynamic chiplet-based heterogeneous architecture with flexible interconnect that adapts compute resource allocation to varying AI workload requirements.
contributions: Heterogeneous chiplet integration combining GPU, NPU, and CPU for flexible compute allocation
Flexible interconnect architecture enabling dynamic workload adaptation
1.8x improvement in performance per watt compared to monolithic designs
Demonstrated efficiency gains across diverse AI applications
limitations: Specific design tradeoffs, flexibility overhead, and scalability limitations not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: heterogeneous chiplet architecture for adaptive AI execution
